brief: A portable electronics organizer: a base with removable bins for small parts, at least one drawer, and a carry handle.

requirements.requirement: A base for an electronics organizer, compact enough to be portable
requirements.evidence: The base is three cells (piece:0,0,0, piece:1,0,0, piece:0,1,0) with 29 parts, under the 30-part limit I set. The size is checked, but the configurator can't check weight or strength.
Two drop-in hex-bin-full-div3 bins (bin:0,0,0 and bin:1,0,0) hold M3 screws, nuts and standoffs. The bin at 0,0,0 sits under the handle cover, so you lift the cover to get at it.
drawer:0#0,1#cut on the half base at 0,1.
handle:0,0,0;top sits on the top cover of cell 0,0,0. The configurator can't check whether it can take the load.

finish.summary:
I built a 3-cell organizer with 29 parts. There are two full hex bases, each holding a removable 3-compartment bin. A north-half base holds a drawer, which opens from its cut face. One bin cell has a top cover with a carry handle on it. I capped the open faces and bolted the joints together. check_build found no rule issues and the mesh check came back clear.

The bins are dressed with props: M3 screws, nuts and standoffs. The two props in the bin under the handle cover can't be seen until you lift the cover. The drawer is empty because the small-parts heaps wouldn't fit in it. I took out a cover I'd added over the drawer cell to bring the count from 32 down to 29 parts, under my 30-part limit for "portable".

Whether the handle and joints are strong enough to carry the loaded organizer depends on the material and how it's printed. The configurator can't check that.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
